paragraphs.en: Come on – Everybody’s doing it. That whispered message, half invitation and half forcing, is what most of us think of when we hear the words peer pressure. It usually leads to no good – drinking, drugs and casual sex. But in her new book Join the Club, Tina Rosenberg contends that peer pressure can also be a positive force through what she calls the social cure, in which organizations and officials use the power of group dynamics to help individuals improve their lives and possibly the world.
paragraphs.zh: “来吧，大家都这么做。”听到“同伴压力”这个词时，我们大多数人想到的，就是这种半是邀请、半是强迫的低声劝说。它通常把人引向不好的行为：酗酒、吸毒以及随意发生性关系。但蒂娜·罗森伯格在新书《加入俱乐部》中主张，通过她所称的“社会疗法”，同伴压力也可以成为一种积极力量：组织和官员可以借助群体互动的力量，帮助个人改善生活，甚至改善世界。

paragraphs.en: Rosenberg, the recipient of a Pulitzer Prize, offers a host of examples of the social cure in action: In South Carolina, a state-sponsored antismoking program called Rage Against the Haze sets out to make cigarettes uncool. In South Africa, an HIV-prevention initiative known as loveLife recruits young people to promote safe sex among their peers.
paragraphs.zh: 普利策奖得主罗森伯格列举了大量社会疗法付诸实践的例子：在南卡罗来纳州，一项名为“怒抗烟霾”、由州政府资助的禁烟计划，着手让抽烟变得不再时髦。在南非，一项名为“热爱生活”的艾滋病预防行动，招募年轻人向同龄人宣传安全性行为。

paragraphs.en: The idea seems promising, and Rosenberg is a perceptive observer. Her critique of the lameness of many public-health campaigns is spot-on: they fail to mobilize peer pressure for healthy habits, and they demonstrate a seriously flawed understanding of psychology. “Dare to be different, please don’t smoke!” pleads one billboard campaign aimed at reducing smoking among teenagers – teenagers, who desire nothing more than fitting in. Rosenberg argues convincingly that public-health advocates ought to take a page from advertisers, so skilled at applying peer pressure.
paragraphs.zh: 这个想法似乎前景不错，罗森伯格也是一位观察敏锐的人。她对许多公共卫生宣传活动效果不佳的批评一针见血：这些活动未能调动同伴压力来培养健康习惯，而且表现出对心理学的严重误解。一项旨在减少青少年吸烟的广告牌宣传活动恳求道：“敢于与众不同，请不要吸烟！”可青少年最渴望的，恰恰是融入群体。罗森伯格很有说服力地指出，公共卫生倡导者应该向那些娴熟运用同伴压力的广告商取经。

paragraphs.en: But on the general effectiveness of the social cure, Rosenberg is less persuasive. Join the Club is filled with too much irrelevant detail and not enough exploration of the social and biological factors that make peer pressure so powerful. The most glaring flaw of the social cure as it’s presented here is that it doesn’t work very well for very long. Rage Against the Haze failed once state funding was cut. Evidence that the loveLife program produces lasting changes is limited and mixed.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，谈到社会疗法的总体成效，罗森伯格就不那么有说服力了。《加入俱乐部》充斥着过多无关细节，却没有充分探讨使同伴压力如此强大的社会和生物学因素。书中所介绍的社会疗法最明显的缺陷是：它难以长期保持良好效果。州政府一削减资助，“怒抗烟霾”计划就失败了。证明“热爱生活”计划能够带来持久变化的证据不仅有限，而且结论也不一致。

paragraphs.en: There’s no doubt that our peer groups exert enormous influence on our behavior. An emerging body of research shows that positive health habits – as well as negative ones – spread through networks of friends via social communication. This is a subtle form of peer pressure: we unconsciously imitate the behavior we see every day.
paragraphs.zh: 毫无疑问，我们的同伴群体对我们的行为有着巨大的影响。越来越多的研究表明，良好的健康习惯和不良习惯一样，会借助社会交往在朋友网络中传播。这是一种微妙的同伴压力：我们会不自觉地模仿每天看到的行为。

paragraphs.en: Far less certain, however, is how successfully experts and bureaucrats can select our peer groups and steer their activities in virtuous directions. It’s like the teacher who breaks up the troublemakers in the back row by pairing them with better-behaved classmates. The tactic never really works. And that’s the problem with a social cure engineered from the outside: in the real world, as in school, we insist on choosing our own friends.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，专家和官僚究竟能在多大程度上成功地替我们选择同伴群体，并引导其活动朝有益的方向发展，就远没有那么确定了。这就像老师把后排捣乱的学生拆开，让他们与表现较好的同学结成对子。这种策略从来没有真正奏效过。由外部设计的社会疗法，问题就在这里：现实世界与学校一样，我们坚持自己选择朋友。
